test_title: PYST 7: SSC CGL 2025 Tier-I Similar Paper - General Awareness (Held On: 14th Sep 2025 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: How are Money Bills treated in the Houses of Parliament and State Legislatures with a bicameral system?

options.text: Rajya Sabha must approve them within 14 days
State Legislative Councils can amend them within 14 days
Both Houses have equal authority over them
Rajya Sabha and State Councils may only recommend changes within 14 days

solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajya Sabha and State Councils may only recommend changes within 14 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Money Bill** is defined under **Article 110** of the **Indian Constitution**. It deals exclusively with matters like **taxation, borrowing, expenditure, or revenue collection** by the government.
 
• **Rajya Sabha's role:** The **Rajya Sabha** does not have the power to reject or amend a Money Bill. It can only provide recommendations within **14 days**. The Lok Sabha may accept or reject these recommendations. If no action is taken by the Rajya Sabha within the prescribed period, the bill is considered passed in its original form. *Hence, the statement "Rajya Sabha must approve them within 14 days" is incorrect.*
 
• **State Legislative Councils:** In states with a bicameral legislature, the **State Legislative Council** (Upper House) functions similarly to the Rajya Sabha. The Council can only recommend changes to a Money Bill and must return it to the State Legislative Assembly within **14 days**. The Assembly may accept or reject these recommendations. *Hence, the statement "State Legislative Councils can amend them within 14 days" is incorrect.*
 
• The assertion that **both Houses have equal authority** over Money Bills is incorrect. In the case of Money Bills, the **Lok Sabha** or the **State Legislative Assembly** has the final authority, and the Upper House (Rajya Sabha or Legislative Council) cannot modify or reject them. *Hence, this statement is also incorrect.*
 
• The correct treatment of a Money Bill is as follows: The **Rajya Sabha** or the **State Legislative Council** can only recommend changes to a Money Bill within **14 days**. They cannot amend or reject it. The final decision rests with the **Lok Sabha** or the **State Legislative Assembly**. *Hence, the correct answer is "Rajya Sabha and State Councils may only recommend changes within 14 days."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Money Bill Features:**

 
 
• A bill is classified as a **Money Bill** if it deals exclusively with financial matters such as **taxation, government borrowing, expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, or appropriation of funds.**
 
• The decision on whether a bill is a Money Bill is made by the **Speaker of the Lok Sabha**, and this decision is final.
 
 
 
• **Procedure for Passing a Money Bill:**
 
 
• A Money Bill can only be introduced in the **Lok Sabha** or the **State Legislative Assembly** (in states with a bicameral legislature).
 
• Once passed in the **Lok Sabha**, it is sent to the **Rajya Sabha**, which may provide recommendations within 14 days. The Lok Sabha may accept or reject these recommendations.
 
• If the Rajya Sabha does not act within 14 days, the bill is deemed to have been passed in its original form by both Houses.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Money Bills:**
 
 
• The **Finance Bill**, which includes the government's annual budget proposals, is a Money Bill.
 
• Other examples include bills related to **taxation laws** and **appropriation of funds** from the Consolidated Fund of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Speaker:**

 
 
• The **Speaker of the Lok Sabha** has the authority to certify whether a bill is a Money Bill, and their decision is final.
 
• The Speaker's certification ensures that the **Rajya Sabha cannot delay or amend Money Bills**.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of the Upper House:**
 
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** or **State Legislative Council** cannot amend or reject a Money Bill; they may only provide recommendations.
 
• The final authority lies with the **Lok Sabha** or the **State Legislative Assembly**.
